You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

So output = all regions filled with the pattern of the first region above the separator? Region1 original is "5 5 5 / 5 5 5", but output region1 is "5 5 5 / 5 3 5" — the pattern of the second region. So output: all regions get the pattern of... region 2 (the one with 3)? Hmm output regions all = "5 5 5 / 5 3 5". Region2 input was "5 5 5 / 5 3 5". So all regions become region2's pattern? Or all become the pattern containing the odd/rare color?

Alternatively: the special content (color 3) replicates to all regions at same relative position. That matches task_36bfa258-style: mark in region map.

Now test input: 9x9, separator row 4 (color 0). Regions: rows 0-3 (4x9) top, rows 5-8 (4x9) bottom. Top region has scattered colors: 8,5,2,1,6,1,6,3,7,7,8 etc. Bottom all 9s. Rule: copy top region into bottom? Output would be 9x9 where bottom rows = top rows replicated? In demo, all regions equal region with content. But which? In demo, region1 (first) was blank and region2 had content; output replicated content everywhere. So rule: all regions take the pattern of the region with non-background content (or the content propagates).

Here top region has content, bottom blank. So output = top region in both? Output 9x9: rows 0-3 = top, row4 = separator 0s, rows 5-8 = top rows repeated.

But maybe only the "special" cells propagate. In demo, whole region pattern copied (5s and 3). Since regions were blank-with-5s, copying region pattern = copying non-bg cells. Here top region has many non-9 cells. Simplest: bottom region = copy of top region.

But is background 9? Top has 9s too. Copy entire top block to bottom. Output rows 5-8 = rows 0-3.

Alternatively could be the 36bfa258 rule: output = small map with one cell per region containing the "mark". But here only 2 regions and output likely 9x9... In demo output same size as input, so propagate.

Submit: rows 0-3 as-is, row4 zeros, rows 5-8 = rows 0-3.

Demo analysis: two regions separated by full separator rows; the region containing the special content (color 3) is replicated into all regions at the same relative position, with the pattern copied wholesale. Applying to the test: top region (rows 0–3) has content, bottom (rows 5–8) is blank, so the bottom becomes a copy of the top.
